title: Hideki Yukawa's birth chart
metaDescription: Hideki Yukawa's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 2.0° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 21.5° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Aquarius, but precisely: 2.0°, first decan, 0°–10°, under Saturn in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Capricorn (24.9°), Venus in Sagittarius (16.5°), Mars in Scorpio (22.2°): a mind that trusts the measured and the checked, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate, drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Uranus opposition Neptune, 0.7° of separation. The scheme reads an opposition as a axis to walk, not a fight to win: the chart keeps both ends lit. Behind it, Saturn trine Neptune at 1.7°, and Saturn sextile Uranus at 2.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Four planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Aquarius at 2.0° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; the Moon in Taurus at 21.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Scorpio at 22.2° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Cancer at 2.8° is in exaltation. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 water, 3 earth, 2 air, 1 fire by element and 4 cardinal, 3 fixed, 3 mutable by mode. A water emphasis reads as porousness: the room is registered whole, long before it is analysed in parts. Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.0° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 21.5°.
